Subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M tokens benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Alex — great to meet today, thanks for the time.

Recap + next steps from our discovery:
- Use case: product chat + semantic search for customer support.
- Expected monthly token volume: see attached estimate (rough range 10M–50M tokens/mo).
- Primary asks: predictable unit economics and a target $/1M tokens budget to evaluate vendor TCO.

To unblock procurement, could you confirm:
1) Target price range you're hoping to hit (e.g., $/1M tokens).
2) Whether you prefer hosted API or reserved/dedicated capacity for consistent SLA.

Attached: acme-token-usage-estimate.csv (your team’s rough monthly projections).

I also attached a quick Redwood vs comps worksheet (redwood-1M-token-price-comparison.xlsx) that walks through our hosted list price and an indicative dedicated pricing band — happy to iterate once you share the target price.

If it helps, propose a short follow-up tomorrow to align on target $/1M and discount runway (6–12 mo) — available 9–11am PT.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M tokens benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Thanks Vanessa — good convo.

Quick answers:
- Target price: our procurement target is ~$30 / 1M tokens as a blended metric. That’s the number we’d need to hit to greenlight a pilot across our EU+US user base.
- Volume: initial pilot monthly run-rate expected ~10–15M tokens, ramp to 40–50M over 6–9 months if perf + quality hold.
- Deployment preference: preferably dedicated/reserved for data isolation and consistent tail latency.

Competitor context for us (benchmarks we’re using internally):
- OpenAI (hosted): we see list ~60–80 $/1M for the higher-cap models we evaluate.
- Anthropic (hosted): ~50–70 $/1M.
- Some self-host/open-host providers: 20–40 $/1M depending on quantization & infra.

We’d like a short proposal showing Redwood dedicated pricing to reach our $30 /1M target (or, if not possible, a clear break-even we can present to finance).

Cc’ing procurement.

—Alex

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M tokens benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Alex — thanks for the clarity and the benchmarks, very helpful.

High-level: based on the volumes you quoted, we can structure a Dedicated reserved band that gets in the neighborhood of your $30 /1M target with a multi-month commit + quantization guidance. Quick illustrative comparison (hosted list vs indicative dedicated band):

- OpenAI (hosted comps): ~60–80 $/1M
- Anthropic (hosted comps): ~50–70 $/1M
- Typical open-model hosts (self-hosted / infra-optimized): ~20–40 $/1M
- Redwood hosted list: ~40 $/1M
- Redwood Dedicated (indicative, with 6–12mo commit + model-optimization): ~25–35 $/1M

I’ve attached the RBC (redwood-1M-token-price-comparison.xlsx) — it includes line items for model family, expected tokens per request, and projected unit costs after batching & KV-cache effects. If you’re targeting $30 /1M, feasible paths:

1) Dedicated 12‑month commit with staged ramp — target ~25–30 $/1M.
2) 6‑month pilot with higher initial rate plus an automatic reprice to meet $30 once you hit the 40M+ run-rate.

Next step: I’ll pull together a short proposal (pricing bands + SLA/dedicated sizing) and include a one‑page cost comparison you can share with finance/procurement. Any constraints from your side on commitment length?

Best,

Vanessa

Attachment(s): redwood-1M-token-price-comparison.xlsx
